title: Copilot Studio: SharePoint lists as an agent knowledge source
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, maker-selected use and documented controls are supported. Minor corrections should clarify differing Microsoft descriptions of freshness and prerequisites, channel restrictions on licence coverage, and the agent limit's exclusion of agent flows.

claims.claim: Learn already documents list knowledge for both standard-harness and Microsoft Copilot harness agents.
claims.quote: After you connect SharePoint lists to your Copilot Studio agent, it can answer questions grounded in structured SharePoint data.

claims.claim: A maker opens the agent, selects Add knowledge, then SharePoint under Upload file, and browses for a list or enters its URL.
claims.quote: 1. Open the agent. 2. Select Add knowledge from either the Overview or Knowledge pages, or the Properties of a generative answers node. 3. In the Upload file section, select SharePoint. 4. Select Browse items to find your desired list, or enter the URL of a specific SharePoint list.

claims.quote: The selected SharePoint lists are ingested into Dataverse and indexed to improve search results.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk

claims.claim: Learn describes the list connection as real-time.
claims.quote: When you add a SharePoint list as a knowledge source, you create a real-time connection to the source, so the most current data is used for queries and reasoning.
claims.fix: After the real-time statement add: 'However, the Unstructured data as a knowledge source FAQ also supports lists through the file-upload route and describes that route as synchronizing content every four to six hours; Microsoft's descriptions of freshness differ.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/knowledge-unstructured-data#faq, whose Runtime differences table gives both list support and that interval.

claims.claim: Users authenticate with their SharePoint credentials.
claims.quote: Users authenticate by using their SharePoint credentials, which ensures they have permission to access the data before your agent provides a response.

claims.quote: This preview supports large-scale lists.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Copilot harness page lists up to 10 lists per agent.

claims.quote: For the best results, only use up to 10 lists per agent.

Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/knowledge-unstructured-data#limits-and-limitations. Retain the supported SharePoint Read-permission statement.

claims.quote: Standard harness agents | Yes, in Microsoft 365 channels | Billed when the user has no Microsoft 365 Copilot license, or when the agent is used in a channel outside Microsoft 365. Microsoft Copilot harness agents | No | Billed for all usage.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Cost and licensing: Caps; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: An agent's monthly Copilot Credit limit can turn off that agent at the defined limit.
claims.quote: Hard stop: The agent is automatically turned off once it hits the defined limit.
claims.fix: After the hard-stop sentence in Caps add: 'An agent's monthly limit does not stop the agent flows it calls; those flows are billed and checked for capacity separately.' The cited https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/manage-copilot-studio-copilot-credits-capacity explicitly states this qualification. Retain the claim that the limit turns off the agent.

claims.claim: Agent limits are not applied instantly.
claims.quote: Limits aren't applied instantly. An agent can continue to respond for some time after it reaches its limit

claims.claim: An environment allocation does not bound consumption when the environment can draw on tenant capacity or pay-as-you-go.
claims.quote: An allocation isn't a boundary if the environment can continue drawing from tenant capacity or pay-as-you-go billing.

claims.claim: Azure budgets provide alerts but do not stop Copilot Studio consumption.
claims.quote: Azure budgets and alerts send notifications but don't stop Copilot Studio consumption.

claims.claim: The PPAC path is Security > Data and privacy > Knowledge sources for agents > Environment groups > environment group > Manage knowledge sources > SharePoint + OneDrive.
claims.quote: select Security. Select the Data and privacy setting. Select the Knowledge sources for agents setting. ... choose whether to sort by Environment groups or by Environments. ... select Manage knowledge sources. ... SharePoint + OneDrive

claims.claim: The SharePoint + OneDrive rule governs the Upload files > SharePoint route used to add lists.
claims.quote: Upload files > SharePoint | SharePoint + OneDrive | Configures whether agents can use SharePoint and OneDrive sites as knowledge sources.

claims.claim: The rule can be configured at environment-group scope.
claims.quote: This setting is available at both the environment and environment group level.

claims.claim: The same setting can be configured for an environment by choosing Environments.
claims.quote: In the side pane, choose whether to sort by Environment groups or by Environments. Select the environment group or environment that you want to configure.

claims.claim: The None option disallows SharePoint and OneDrive sites as knowledge sources.
claims.quote: None: Don't use any SharePoint and OneDrive sites as knowledge sources.

claims.claim: The All option permits SharePoint and OneDrive sites as knowledge sources.
claims.quote: All: Use all SharePoint and OneDrive sites as knowledge sources.

claims.claim: Custom allows or denies SharePoint and OneDrive sites by URL.
claims.quote: Custom: Select which SharePoint and OneDrive sites agents can use. Agents reference them in priority order, starting with the first URL. Select either Allow or Deny under Access for each URL.

claims.claim: The Knowledge sources for agents documentation is marked preview.
claims.quote: Configure knowledge sources for agents in the Power Platform admin center (preview). [This article is prerelease documentation and is subject to change.]

claims.claim: A group-level configuration cannot be changed at the environment level.
claims.quote: if an admin sets the control at the environment group level, then it's distributed to the environment level and can't be modified there.

claims.claim: Power Platform administrators configure environment-group rules.
claims.quote: After you create the environment group, Power Platform tenant administrators can immediately add managed environments or configure the group's rules.

claims.claim: The PPAC path Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Summary > Manage Agents reaches the page containing monthly agent limits.

claims.claim: On Manage Agents, select the agent and then Set limit to enter a monthly credit limit.
claims.quote: Select the agent, and then select Set limit. Enter the monthly Copilot Credit limit.

claims.claim: Turn on Stop usage to turn off the agent when its limit is reached.

claims.claim: Monthly limits apply per Copilot Studio agent generally, not only to list knowledge or one harness.
claims.quote: Admins can set monthly consumption limits for each Copilot Studio agent, regardless of whether the environment uses prepaid capacity or pay-as-you-go billing.

claims.claim: Manage Agents shows month-to-date billed credits.
